soc_summary: Venetoclax + hypomethylating agent has been FDA-approved for newly diagnosed AML in patients aged 75+ or unfit for intensive chemotherapy since 2018 and is a guideline first-line option, so the comparator is routinely available outside trials.
regulatory_summary: FDA IND plus IRB/site contracting. KMR benchmark: North America has the shortest start-up cycle time of any region (4.1 months), though activating many US sites can take much longer after the first one.
recruitment_notes: Largest acute-leukemia site base, but also the most crowded: about 200 recruiting acute leukemia trials have US sites (ClinicalTrials.gov pull in the tool). Comparator access offers little enrollment incentive.

soc_summary: NICE TA765 (Feb 2022) recommends venetoclax + azacitidine for untreated AML when intensive chemotherapy is unsuitable, within its marketing authorisation and subject to the commercial arrangement. NICE estimated about 650 eligible patients.
regulatory_summary: MHRA plus HRA/REC approval. No citable country-specific start-up benchmark was found, so the tool default applies.
recruitment_notes: Comparator is NHS standard of care for unfit AML, so randomization offers little access incentive. Eligible population per NICE is modest (~650/year).

soc_summary: G-BA (Dec 2021) found an indication of considerable added benefit for venetoclax + azacitidine over azacitidine in newly diagnosed AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy. The DGHO describes the combination as the new standard for this population, and it is reimbursed by statutory insurance.
regulatory_summary: EU-CTR (CTIS) authorisation plus ethics review. No citable country-specific start-up benchmark was found, so the tool default applies.
recruitment_notes: Comparator is routine standard of care, so it offers little enrollment incentive. Germany has one of the largest experienced acute leukemia site bases in Europe.

soc_summary: HAS Transparency Committee (June 2021): SMR important and ASMR III (moderate improvement) for venetoclax + azacitidine in newly diagnosed AML ineligible for intensive induction. Reimbursement applies only to the azacitidine combination.
regulatory_summary: EU-CTR (CTIS) authorisation plus CPP ethics review. No citable country-specific start-up benchmark was found, so the tool default applies.
recruitment_notes: Comparator is reimbursed standard of care. Note that HAS restricts reimbursement to the azacitidine combination, not other HMAs.

soc_summary: AIFA Determina 248/2023 (GU 1 April 2023): venetoclax + azacitidine reimbursed by the SSN (class H, AIFA monitoring registry) for adults with newly diagnosed AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy, from 2 April 2023. Earlier access was via Law 648/96 for relapsed/refractory AML.
regulatory_summary: EU-CTR (CTIS) authorisation plus ethics review. No citable country-specific start-up benchmark was found, so the tool default applies.
recruitment_notes: Comparator is reimbursed in routine care, but prescribing is limited to hospital haematology centres with an AIFA registry.

soc_summary: Venetoclax with an HMA is authorised for newly diagnosed AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy (AEMPS label), and Andalusia's GHEMA hospital evaluation covers venetoclax + azacitidine. No national SNS financing decision or IPT for the AML indication was found; access may vary by region.
regulatory_summary: EU-CTR (CTIS) authorisation plus CEIm ethics review. No citable country-specific start-up benchmark was found, so the tool default applies.
recruitment_notes: If national financing is restricted or regional, trial access to the comparator could be an enrollment incentive. Verify with local affiliates.

soc_summary: CADTH/pCODR (Aug 2021) recommended reimbursing venetoclax + azacitidine with conditions: newly diagnosed AML aged 75+ or with comorbidities precluding intensive chemotherapy, prescriber expertise, and a price reduction. Coverage is provincial (e.g., Cancer Care Ontario listing).
regulatory_summary: Health Canada CTA (30-day review) plus REB approval. No citable country-specific start-up benchmark was found, so the tool default applies.
recruitment_notes: Conditional, province-by-province coverage leaves some patients without routine access, which gives the comparator modest incentive value.

soc_summary: Venetoclax + azacitidine was PBS-listed for AML from 1 December 2021, cutting patient cost from over $88,000 per course to standard co-payments. The Leukaemia Foundation estimated about 340 eligible patients per year.
regulatory_summary: CTN/CTA scheme plus HREC approval. No citable country-specific start-up benchmark for late-phase trials was found, so the tool default applies.
recruitment_notes: Comparator is fully reimbursed, so it offers little access incentive. The eligible pool is small (~340/year).

soc_summary: Since 1 September 2022, AML drug programme B.114 reimburses venetoclax + azacitidine first-line, alongside midostaurin, gemtuzumab ozogamicin and (in newer versions) ivosidenib, oral azacitidine and gilteritinib. Access runs through programme centres with eligibility criteria. Before 2022, patients had almost no modern options.
regulatory_summary: EU-CTR (CTIS) authorisation. A Polish CRO guide puts typical start-up at 3–6 months (7–9 for complex projects); 4.5 months used as the midpoint.
recruitment_notes: Lower saturation than Western Europe (about 0.4 recruiting trials per known site in the registry pull). Programme-based access means some patients reach the comparator later, which gives it some incentive value.

soc_summary: Since February 2023, venetoclax + decitabine or azacitidine is reimbursed first-line only for newly diagnosed AML patients aged 75+ who are unfit for induction chemotherapy, under a risk-sharing agreement renewed in July 2024.
regulatory_summary: MFDS IND plus IRB. No citable country-specific start-up benchmark was found, so the tool default applies.
recruitment_notes: Unfit patients under 75 lack reimbursed access, so trial access to venetoclax is a meaningful incentive for that group. Major academic centres (SNUH, Samsung, Severance) are experienced in venetoclax AML studies.

soc_summary: MHLW granted venetoclax orphan designation for AML in June 2020, and VIALE-A Japanese subgroup data support venetoclax + azacitidine as first-line standard of care for unfit patients. The AML approval date and NHI listing could not be confirmed from the sources found.
regulatory_summary: PMDA Clinical Trial Notification (30-day review for initial submissions) plus IRB. KMR benchmark: Japan start-up cycle 5.4 months, shorter than average.
recruitment_notes: Low saturation in the registry pull (about 0.35 recruiting trials per known site) and a large experienced site base. Japanese participation is often needed for PMDA filing.

soc_summary: Venetoclax was approved in China in December 2020 for older or unfit AML patients, and in-hospital sales exceeded RMB 1.5 billion in 2023 (secondary source), indicating wide use. National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL) status for AML could not be confirmed from the sources found.
regulatory_summary: NMPA CTA under a 60-working-day implied-approval clock (30-working-day fast track since 2025 for qualifying innovative drugs), plus Human Genetic Resources filing or approval, ethics review and hospital contracting. Total start-up months could not be quantified from current sources.
recruitment_notes: Very crowded: about 188 recruiting acute leukemia trials have Chinese sites (1.4 per known site in the registry pull), concentrated in large haematology centres.
